sanskrit: taṃ pitā paramakruddho yayātir nahuṣātmajaḥ śaśāpa putraṃ gāndhāre rājyāc ca vyaparopayat
english: His father Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, in extreme fury cursed that son, O Gāndhāra king, and removed him from the kingdom.

sanskrit: ya cainam anvavartanta bhrātaro baladarpitam śaśāpa tān api kruddho yayātis tanayān atha
english: And those brothers who followed him in his arrogant pride — Yayāti, enraged, cursed those sons as well.

sanskrit: yavīyāṃsaṃ tataḥ pūruṃ putraṃ svavaśavartinam rājye niveśayām āsa vidheyaṃ nṛpasattamaḥ
english: Then that best of kings installed his younger son Pūru, who was obedient and compliant, upon the throne.

sanskrit: evaṃ jyeṣṭho 'py athotsikto na rājyam abhijāyate yavīyāṃso 'bhijāyante rājyaṃ vṛddhopasevayā
english: Thus even a proud elder son does not obtain the kingdom, while younger sons obtain it through service to the elders.

sanskrit: tathaiva sarvadharmajñaḥ pitur mama pitāmahaḥ pratīpaḥ pṛthivīpālas triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ
english: Similarly, my father's grandfather Pratīpa, the earth-protector, knower of all dharma, was renowned in all three worlds.

sanskrit: tasya pārthivasiṃhasya rājyaṃ dharmeṇa śāsataḥ trayaḥ prajajñire putrā devakalpā yaśasvinaḥ
english: Of that lion among kings, ruling his kingdom righteously, three illustrious sons were born, equal to the gods in glory.

sanskrit: devāpir abhavaj jyeṣṭho bāhlīkas tadanantaram tṛtīyaḥ śaṃtanus tāta dhṛtimān me pitāmahaḥ
english: Devāpi was the eldest, Bāhlīka came next, and the third, O father, was the steadfast Śaṃtanu, my grandfather.

sanskrit: devāpis tu mahātejās tvagdoṣī rājasattamaḥ dhārmikaḥ satyavādī ca pituḥ śuśrūṣaṇe rataḥ
english: But Devāpi, though of great splendor and best of kings, had a skin disease; he was righteous, truthful, and devoted to serving his father.

sanskrit: paurajānapadānāṃ ca saṃmataḥ sādhusatkṛtaḥ sarveṣāṃ bālavṛddhānāṃ devāpir hṛdayaṃgamaḥ
english: Devāpi was honored by the people of the city and countryside, respected by the virtuous, and dear to the hearts of all — young and old alike.

sanskrit: prājñaś ca satyasaṃdhaś ca sarvabhūtahite rataḥ vartamānaḥ pituḥ śāstre brāhmaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca
english: He was wise, true to his word, devoted to the welfare of all beings, and lived by the teachings of his father and the brahmaṇas.

sanskrit: bāhlīkasya priyo bhrātā śaṃtanoś ca mahātmanaḥ saubhrātraṃ ca paraṃ teṣāṃ sahitānāṃ mahātmanām
english: He was dear as a brother to Bāhlīka and to the great-souled Śaṃtanu, and there was supreme fraternal harmony among those noble souls united together.

sanskrit: atha kālasya paryāye vṛddho nṛpatisattamaḥ saṃbhārān abhiṣekārthaṃ kārayām āsa śāstrataḥ maṅgalāni ca sarvāṇi kārayām āsa cābhibhūḥ
english: Then in the course of time, the aged king, that best of rulers, had the materials for the consecration prepared according to scripture, and had all the auspicious rites performed as well — he who was sovereign over all.

sanskrit: taṃ brāhmaṇāś ca vṛddhāś ca paurajānapadaiḥ saha sarve nivārayām āsur devāper abhiṣecanam
english: But the brahmaṇas and elders, together with the people of city and countryside, all prevented the consecration of Devāpi.

sanskrit: sa tac chrutvā tu nṛpatir abhiṣekanivāraṇam aśrukaṇṭho 'bhavad rājā paryaśocata cātmajam
english: Hearing that the consecration was barred, the king's throat choked with tears, and he grieved deeply for his son.

sanskrit: evaṃ vadānyo dharmajñaḥ satyasaṃdhaś ca so 'bhavat priyaḥ prajānām api saṃs tvagdoṣeṇa pradūṣitaḥ
english: Although so generous, so learned in dharma, so true to his vow, and so dear to the people, he was disqualified by the blemish of a skin disease.

sanskrit: hīnāṅgaṃ pṛthivīpālaṃ nābhinandanti devatāḥ iti kṛtvā nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ pratyaṣedhan dvijarṣabhāḥ
english: "The gods do not favor a king with a bodily defect" — on this ground the foremost of twice-born men barred that best of kings.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravyathitātmāsau putraśokasamanvitaḥ mamāra taṃ mṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā devāpiḥ saṃśrito vanam
english: Then that king, his soul deeply troubled and grief-stricken for his son, died; and seeing him dead, Devāpi took refuge in the forest.

sanskrit: bāhlīko mātulakule tyaktvā rājyaṃ vyavasthitaḥ pitṛbhrātṝn parityajya prāptavān puram ṛddhimat
english: Bāhlīka, abandoning the kingdom, settled in his mother's family, renouncing his father's brothers, and attained a prosperous city.

sanskrit: bāhlīkena tv anujñātaḥ śaṃtanur lokaviśrutaḥ pitary uparate rājan rājā rājyam akārayat
english: With Bāhlīka's permission, O king, the world-renowned Śaṃtanu ruled the kingdom as king after his father's death.

sanskrit: tathaivāhaṃ matimatā paricintyeha pāṇḍunā jyeṣṭhaḥ prabhraṃśito rājyād dhīnāṅga iti bhārata
english: In the same way, O Bhārata, I — the elder — was removed from the kingdom by the wise Pāṇḍu on the ground that I am defective in a limb.

sanskrit: pāṇḍus tu rājyaṃ saṃprāptaḥ kanīyān api san nṛpaḥ vināśe tasya putrāṇām idaṃ rājyam ariṃdama mayy abhāgini rājyāya kathaṃ tvaṃ rājyam icchasi
english: Pāṇḍu, though younger, obtained the kingdom as king. Now with his sons destroyed, this kingdom belongs here; I am unfit for kingship — how then, O subduer of foes, can you desire this kingdom?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro rājaputro mahātmā; nyāyāgataṃ rājyam idaṃ ca tasya sa kauravasyāsya janasya bhartā; praśāsitā caiva mahānubhāvaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira is a noble prince of great soul; this kingdom has come to him by rightful succession. He is the lord of this Kaurava people, and a ruler of great majesty.

sanskrit: sa satyasaṃdhaḥ satatāpramattaḥ; śāstre sthito bandhujanasya sādhuḥ priyaḥ prajānāṃ suhṛdānukampī; jitendriyaḥ sādhujanasya bhartā
english: He is true to his vow, ever vigilant, steadfast in his duty, virtuous toward his kin, beloved of the people, compassionate to friends, master of his senses, and protector of the good.

sanskrit: kṣamā titikṣā dama ārjavaṃ ca; satyavratatvaṃ śrutam apramādaḥ bhūtānukampā hy anuśāsanaṃ ca; yudhiṣṭhire rājaguṇāḥ samastāḥ
english: Forbearance, patience, self-control, uprightness, adherence to the vow of truth, learning, heedfulness, compassion for all beings, and the power of command — all the virtues of a king are united in Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: arājaputras tvam anāryavṛtto; lubdhas tathā bandhuṣu pāpabuddhiḥ kramāgataṃ rājyam idaṃ pareṣāṃ; hartuṃ kathaṃ śakṣyasi durvinītaḥ
english: You are no true prince, you follow ignoble conduct, you are greedy, you harbor wicked thoughts toward your own kin — how can you, so ill-behaved, seize this kingdom that belongs by succession to another?

sanskrit: prayaccha rājyārdham apetamohaḥ; savāhanaṃ tvaṃ saparicchadaṃ ca tato 'vaśeṣaṃ tava jīvitasya; sahānujasyaiva bhaven narendra
english: Free yourself from delusion and give up half the kingdom — with its cavalry and all its furnishings. Then the remainder of your life, together with your brother's, may still be secured, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca evam ukte tu bhīṣmeṇa droṇena vidureṇa ca gāndhāryā dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa na ca mando 'nvabudhyata
english: Vāsudeva said: Though Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Vidura, Gāndhārī, and Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke thus, the foolish one did not come to his senses.

sanskrit: avadhūyotthitaḥ kruddho roṣāt saṃraktalocanaḥ anvadravanta taṃ paścād rājānas tyaktajīvitāḥ
english: He shook off their words, rose up in anger, his eyes red with rage; and the kings, reckless of their lives, ran after him.

sanskrit: ajñāpayac ca rājñas tān pārthivān duṣṭacetasaḥ prayādhvaṃ vai kurukṣetraṃ puṣyo 'dyeti punaḥ punaḥ
english: And that evil-minded king commanded those rulers again and again: "March to Kurukṣetra — today is the auspicious Puṣya asterism!"

sanskrit: tatas te pṛthivīpālāḥ prayayuḥ sahasainikāḥ bhīṣmaṃ senāpatiṃ kṛtvā saṃhṛṣṭāḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: Then those lords of the earth marched out with their armies, making Bhīṣma their commander, rejoicing, driven on by fate.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyo daśaikā ca pārthivānāṃ samāgatāḥ tāsāṃ pramukhato bhīṣmas tālaketur vyarocata yad atra yuktaṃ prāptaṃ ca tad vidhatsva viśāṃ pate
english: Eleven akṣauhiṇī armies of the kings assembled; at their head Bhīṣma, bearing the palm-tree banner, shone resplendent. Do now, O lord of the earth, whatever is fitting and proper here.

sanskrit: uktaṃ bhīṣmeṇa yad vākyaṃ droṇena vidureṇa ca gāndhāryā dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa samakṣaṃ mama bhārata etat te kathitaṃ rājan yadvṛttaṃ kurusaṃsadi
english: O Bhārata, the words spoken by Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Vidura, Gāndhārī, and Dhṛtarāṣṭra in my presence — all that transpired in the Kuru assembly, O king, I have now told you.

sanskrit: sāma ādau prayuktaṃ me rājan saubhrātram icchatā abhedāt kuruvaṃśasya prajānāṃ ca vivṛddhaye
english: Conciliation was first employed by me, O king, as I desired brotherly harmony — for the preservation of the unity of the Kuru lineage and the prosperity of the people.

sanskrit: punar bhedaś ca me yukto yadā sāma na gṛhyate karmānukīrtanaṃ caiva devamānuṣasaṃhitam
english: Then division too was my instrument when conciliation was not accepted — along with the recounting of deeds that combined the divine and the human.

sanskrit: yadā nādriyate vākyaṃ sāmapūrvaṃ suyodhanaḥ tadā mayā samānīya bheditāḥ sarvapārthivāḥ
english: When Suyodhana did not honor speech beginning with conciliation, then I, having summoned all the kings together, drove them apart.

sanskrit: adbhutāni ca ghorāṇi dāruṇāni ca bhārata amānuṣāṇi karmāṇi darśitāni ca me vibho
english: And I demonstrated marvellous, terrifying, dreadful, superhuman deeds, O Bhārata, O lord.

sanskrit: bhartsayitvā tu rājñas tāṃs tṛṇīkṛtya suyodhanam rādheyaṃ bhīṣayitvā ca saubalaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: And after threatening those kings and making Suyodhana seem as nothing as straw, and frightening Rādheya and Śakuni again and again —

sanskrit: nyūnatāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ nindāṃ caiva punaḥ punaḥ bhedayitvā nṛpān sarvān vāgbhir mantreṇa cāsakṛt
english: — proclaiming again and again the inferiority and censure of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and dividing all the kings through speech and counsel repeatedly —

sanskrit: punaḥ sāmābhisaṃyuktaṃ saṃpradānam athābruvam abhedāt kuruvaṃśasya kāryayogāt tathaiva ca
english: — I then again spoke of conciliation combined with the gift, for the unity of the Kuru lineage and also for the sake of what needed to be done.

sanskrit: te bālā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya bhīṣmasya vidurasya ca tiṣṭheyuḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sarve hitvā mānam adhaścarāḥ
english: "Let all the Pāṇḍavas abide by the words of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Bhīṣma, and Vidura, setting aside pride, and living humbly subordinate."

sanskrit: prayacchantu ca te rājyam anīśās te bhavantu ca yathāha rājā gāṅgeyo viduraś ca tathāstu tat
english: "Let them yield up the kingdom and become powerless, as the river-born king Bhīṣma and Vidura have declared — let it be so."

sanskrit: sarvaṃ bhavatu te rājyaṃ pañca grāmān visarjaya avaśyaṃ bharaṇīyā hi pitus te rājasattama
english: "Let all the kingdom be yours — but give up five villages; for your father's sons must certainly be provided for, O best of kings."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu duṣṭātmā naiva bhāvaṃ vyamuñcata daṇḍaṃ caturthaṃ paśyāmi teṣu pāpeṣu nānyathā
english: But spoken to thus, the evil-souled one did not relent at all. I see the fourth expedient — force — as the only recourse against those sinful ones; there is no other way.

sanskrit: niryātāś ca vināśāya kurukṣetraṃ narādhipāḥ etat te kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yadvṛttaṃ kurusaṃsadi
english: And the lords of men have marched out to Kurukṣetra for their destruction. All that occurred in the Kuru assembly I have now recounted to you.

sanskrit: na te rājyaṃ prayacchanti vinā yuddhena pāṇḍava vināśahetavaḥ sarve pratyupasthitamṛtyavaḥ
english: They will not give you the kingdom without war, O Pāṇḍava. All of them are causes of destruction, with death standing ready before them.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca janārdanavacaḥ śrutvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhrātṝn uvāca dharmātmā samakṣaṃ keśavasya ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Janārdana, the righteous king Yudhiṣṭhira, whose soul was in dharma, spoke to his brothers in the presence of Keśava.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ bhavadbhir yadvṛttaṃ sabhāyāṃ kurusaṃsadi keśavasyāpi yad vākyaṃ tat sarvam avadhāritam
english: "You have all heard what transpired in the assembly of the Kuru council, and every word that Keśava spoke has been well taken in."

sanskrit: tasmāt senāvibhāgaṃ me kurudhvaṃ narasattamāḥ akṣauhiṇyas tu saptaitāḥ sametā vijayāya vai
english: "Therefore, O best of men, carry out for me the division of the army. These seven akṣauhiṇī forces have assembled here for victory."

sanskrit: tāsāṃ me patayaḥ sapta vikhyātās tān nibodhata drupadaś ca virāṭaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinau
english: "The seven commanders of these forces are well known — hear them: Drupada and Virāṭa, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin,"

sanskrit: sātyakiś cekitānaś ca bhīmasenaś ca vīryavān ete senāpraṇetāro vīrāḥ sarve tanutyajaḥ
english: "Sātyaki, Cekitāna, and the mighty Bhīmasena — these are the army's leading heroes, all ready to lay down their lives."

sanskrit: sarve vedavidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve sucaritavratāḥ hrīmanto nītimantaś ca sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ iṣvastrakuśalāś caiva tathā sarvāstrayodhinaḥ
english: "All are versed in the Vedas and valiant, all of pure and observed vows, all endowed with modesty and wisdom, all skilled in battle, expert in archery, and fighters with every weapon."

sanskrit: saptānām api yo netā senānāṃ pravibhāgavit yaḥ saheta raṇe bhīṣmaṃ śarārciḥpāvakopamam
english: "But who shall be the one leader over all seven armies, skilled in their distribution — one who in battle could withstand Bhīṣma, who is like a blazing fire of arrows?"

sanskrit: tvaṃ tāvat sahadevātra prabrūhi kurunandana svamataṃ puruṣavyāghra ko naḥ senāpatiḥ kṣamaḥ
english: "You, Sahadeva, speak up here, O delight of the Kurus, tiger among men — tell us your opinion: who is fit to be our commander?"

sanskrit: sahadeva uvāca saṃyukta ekaduḥkhaś ca vīryavāṃś ca mahīpatiḥ yaṃ samāśritya dharmajñaṃ svam aṃśam anuyuñjmahe
english: Sahadeva said: He is allied with us, shares in our grief, is mighty, a lord of the earth, a knower of dharma — relying on him we seek to recover our own portion.

sanskrit: matsyo virāṭo balavān kṛtāstro yuddhadurmadaḥ prasahiṣyati saṃgrāme bhīṣmaṃ tāṃś ca mahārathān
english: The Matsya king Virāṭa, strong, skilled in arms, intoxicated with battle-fury — he will be able to withstand Bhīṣma and those great chariot-warriors in combat.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathokte sahadevena vākye vākyaviśāradaḥ nakulo 'nantaraṃ tasmād idaṃ vacanam ādade
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Sahadeva had spoken thus, Nakula, the eloquent in speech, immediately took up the matter after him with these words.

sanskrit: vayasā śāstrato dhairyāt kulenābhijanena ca hrīmān kulānvitaḥ śrīmān sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ
english: "By age, by learning in the scriptures, by steadfastness, by lineage and noble birth, he is endowed with modesty, graced with high family, possessed of glory, expert in all the sacred sciences —"

sanskrit: veda cāstraṃ bharadvājād durdharṣaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ yo nityaṃ spardhate droṇaṃ bhīṣmaṃ caiva mahābalam
english: "— he has learned weaponcraft from Bharadvāja's son, he is indomitable and true to his pledge, and he perpetually rivals Droṇa and the mighty Bhīṣma —"

sanskrit: ślāghyaḥ pārthivasaṃghasya pramukhe vāhinīpatiḥ putrapautraiḥ parivṛtaḥ śataśākha iva drumaḥ
english: "— praiseworthy as the foremost commander before the assembly of kings, surrounded by sons and grandsons like a tree with a hundred branches —"

sanskrit: yas tatāpa tapo ghoraṃ sadāraḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ roṣād droṇavināśāya vīraḥ samitiśobhanaḥ
english: "— that hero and lord of the earth, together with his wife, performed fierce austerities out of fury for the destruction of Droṇa, and he shines in every assembly —"

sanskrit: pitevāsmān samādhatte yaḥ sadā pārthivarṣabhaḥ śvaśuro drupado 'smākaṃ senām agre prakarṣatu
english: "— he who always provides for us like a father, that bull among kings — let our father-in-law Drupada lead the army at the vanguard."

sanskrit: sa droṇabhīṣmāv āyāntau sahed iti matir mama sa hi divyāstravid rājā sakhā cāṅgiraso nṛpaḥ
english: "He, I believe, could withstand both Droṇa and Bhīṣma as they advance in battle — for he is a king who knows divine weapons and is a friend and disciple of the descendant of Aṅgiras."

sanskrit: mādrīsutābhyām ukte tu svamate kurunandanaḥ vāsavir vāsavasamaḥ savyasācy abravīd vacaḥ
english: When the two sons of Mādrī had spoken their views, the son of Vasava, equal to Vasava himself, the left-handed archer Arjuna, spoke up.

sanskrit: yo 'yaṃ tapaḥprabhāvena ṛṣisaṃtoṣaṇena ca divyaḥ puruṣa utpanno jvālāvarṇo mahābalaḥ
english: "He who was born a divine person through the power of austerity and the satisfaction of the sages, blazing in color and of great strength —"

sanskrit: dhanuṣmān kavacī khaḍgī ratham āruhya daṃśitaḥ divyair hayavarair yuktam agnikuṇḍāt samutthitaḥ
english: "— bearing a bow, clad in armor, wielding a sword, mounting his chariot in full battle-gear, drawn by the finest divine horses, risen up from the sacrificial fire-pit —"

sanskrit: garjann iva mahāmegho rathaghoṣeṇa vīryavān siṃhasaṃhanano vīraḥ siṃhavikrāntavikramaḥ
english: "— roaring like a great storm-cloud with the thunder of his chariot, that valiant hero with a lion's build and a lion's mighty stride —"

sanskrit: siṃhorasko mahābāhuḥ siṃhavakṣā mahābalaḥ siṃhapragarjano vīraḥ siṃhaskandho mahādyutiḥ
english: "— lion-chested, long-armed, with a lion's breast and great strength, roaring like a lion, with a lion's shoulders, of great radiance —"

sanskrit: subhrūḥ sudaṃṣṭraḥ suhanuḥ subāhuḥ sumukho 'kṛśaḥ sujatruḥ suviśālākṣaḥ supādaḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: "— with beautiful brows, beautiful teeth, a beautiful jaw, beautiful arms, a beautiful face, not lean, a beautiful clavicle, wide beautiful eyes, beautiful feet, and standing beautifully —"

sanskrit: abhedyaḥ sarvaśastrāṇāṃ prabhinna iva vāraṇaḥ jajñe droṇavināśāya satyavādī jitendriyaḥ
english: "— impenetrable to all weapons, like a rutting elephant in his force, born for the destruction of Droṇa, truthful in speech, master of his senses —"

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnam ahaṃ manye sahed bhīṣmasya sāyakān vajrāśanisamasparśān dīptāsyān uragān iva
english: "— I believe Dhṛṣṭadyumna could withstand Bhīṣma's arrows, which are like the touch of the thunderbolt and lightning, like fire-mouthed serpents —"

sanskrit: yamadūtasamān vege nipāte pāvakopamān rāmeṇājau viṣahitān vajraniṣpeṣadāruṇān
english: "— equal to Yama's messengers in speed and descent, like fire in their fury, borne up even by Rāma in battle, dreadful as the crushing stroke of the thunderbolt —"

sanskrit: puruṣaṃ taṃ na paśyāmi yaḥ saheta mahāvratam dhṛṣṭadyumnam ṛte rājann iti me dhīyate matiḥ
english: "I see no man who could withstand the great-vowed Bhīṣma other than Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O king — such is my considered opinion."

sanskrit: kṣiprahastaś citrayodhī mataḥ senāpatir mama abhedyakavacaḥ śrīmān mātaṅga iva yūthapaḥ
english: "Quick of hand, varied in his fighting — he is my choice for commander, his armor impenetrable, glorious, like a great elephant leading the herd."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca vadhārthaṃ yaḥ samutpannaḥ śikhaṇḍī drupadātmajaḥ vadanti siddhā rājendra ṛṣayaś ca samāgatāḥ
english: Bhīma said: Śikhaṇḍin, son of Drupada, was born for the purpose of killing — so declare the Siddhas and the sages assembled together, O king of kings.

sanskrit: yasya saṃgrāmamadhyeṣu divyam astraṃ vikurvataḥ rūpaṃ drakṣyanti puruṣā rāmasyeva mahātmanaḥ
english: In the midst of battles, when he deploys his divine weapon, men will behold his form as they behold the great-souled Rāma himself.

sanskrit: na taṃ yuddheṣu paśyāmi yo vibhindyāc chikhaṇḍinam śastreṇa samare rājan saṃnaddhaṃ syandane sthitam
english: I see no one in battles, O king, who could pierce Śikhaṇḍin with a weapon in combat, when he stands armored upon his chariot.

sanskrit: dvairathe viṣahen nānyo bhīṣmaṃ rājan mahāvratam śikhaṇḍinam ṛte vīraṃ sa me senāpatir mataḥ
english: None other could withstand Bhīṣma of the great vow in single chariot combat, O king, save the hero Śikhaṇḍin — he is my choice for commander.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sarvasya jagatas tāta sārāsāraṃ balābalam sarvaṃ jānāti dharmātmā gatam eṣyac ca keśavaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O father, the soul of dharma Keśava knows the essence and the non-essence, the strength and weakness, of all the world — past and future alike.

sanskrit: yam āha kṛṣṇo dāśārhaḥ so 'stu no vāhinīpatiḥ kṛtāstro hy akṛtāstro vā vṛddho vā yadi vā yuvā
english: Whoever Kṛṣṇa of the Dāśārha clan names — whether skilled in arms or not, whether old or young — let that one be our commander of the army.

sanskrit: eṣa no vijaye mūlam eṣa tāta viparyaye atra prāṇāś ca rājyaṃ ca bhāvābhāvau sukhāsukhe
english: He is the root of our victory, O father, and of our defeat as well. In him lie our lives and our kingdom, our being and non-being, our joy and sorrow.
